missing_spec_content.spec_text: Work is done when charge flows in a circuit. The amount of energy transferred by electrical work can be calculated using the equation:
missing_spec_content.why: The lesson never states that work is done when charge flows in a circuit, or that this is how appliances transfer energy. It only says, in passing, that E = QV 'links the mechanical 'work done' idea of energy to circuit quantities' (keyPoints[2].content). It also gives a brief analogy in keyPoints[2].tutor_note: 'It is just energy = work done to move charge Q through a potential difference V.' The spec's own statement is never taught directly.

missing_spec_content.spec_text:
energy transferred = charge flow × potential difference

E = Q V ... Students should be able to recall and apply both equations.
missing_spec_content.why: E = QV appears in the lesson as a listed equation. However, the lesson gives no worked example and no checkpoint that applies it. The spec requires students to apply it, not only recall it.

above_gcse.why: Neither specification section asks for fuse ratings or dedicated circuits. These are extra details that the student is not asked to learn here. The shower entry is also wrong (see factual_errors), so it could confuse the student.

factual_errors.correction: An 8–10 kW shower on 230 V mains draws about 35–43 A, since I = P/V. It is therefore not protected by a 13 A fuse. It runs on a dedicated circuit with a protective device of roughly 40–45 A. The lesson's own P = IV shows that 13 A is far too low.

wrong_terms.text: Writing P = IR instead of P = I²R gives the voltage, not the power.
This is the right equation when you have current and resistance but not voltage.
Every time you boil a kettle, stream a video or charge your phone, electrical energy is transferred.
wrong_terms.spec_term: energy transferred by electrical work (work is done when charge flows in a circuit)

checkpoint_mismatch.checkpoint: checkpoints[2]: "A resistor has R = 50 Ω and V = 10 V. What is the energy transferred in 2 minutes?"
checkpoint_mismatch.key_point: keyPoints[2] "Linking all the electrical equations": "Worked multi-step example: a resistor has R = 50 Ω and V = 10 V. Find the energy transferred in 2 minutes. ... 240 J"
checkpoint_mismatch.why: The checkpoint copies the worked example word for word, with the same numbers. It tests whether the student remembers the example, not whether they can apply the method. It also does not test the content this key point adds, which is Q = It and E = QV.

not_checked: Q = It (keyPoints[2].content, tables[0].rows[5], revisionCardBullets[6]) is not in the specification sections supplied (4.2.4.1, 4.2.4.2). Its spec wording and terminology could not be checked against the specification text. It was checked against own knowledge only and is correct.
